hypothesis: The target-absent 'lineup effect' is produced by the response format that demands a PICK, not by simultaneous presentation: with the PICK removed (ACCEPT/REJECT only), simultaneous pools accept wrong hypotheses no more often than isolated calls, and a serial-in-one-prompt arm that keeps the PICK inflates as much as the simultaneous pool.
gap_with_citations: The corpus contains a direct contradiction it never resolved. Arithmetic frontier run (corpus/02-lineup-problem-verifier/frontier-run/results_fn.txt): serial_8 probe f_serial(8)=0.0122 (14/1152) vs simultaneous n=8 per-candidate 0.0874; the serial prompt (judge_prompts.md) has no PICK and says 'do not compare entries to each other'. Hypothesis pilot (corpus/08-hypothesis-lineup-pilot/FINDING.md sec. 3): SERIAL choosing 14/48=0.292, identical to POOL0, and FINDING.md itself names explanation (b): 'the serial prompt still ended with a PICK over the set'. x1/x1c pool prompts (exp/x1-sequential-lineup/build.py) ask for 'PICK: the label of the single best-supported hypothesis, or NONE', a relative instruction absent from ISO. My recount of exp/x1*/raw POOL0 outputs: in x1, x1s, x1f every choosing pool both PICKed and ACCEPTed (x1c: 2 of 42 picks had no ACCEPT), so PICK and ACCEPT are coupled and the PICK demand may drive the ACCEPT. No experiment crosses presentation x format.
prediction: Artifact account: POOL0-noPICK choosing rate within 0.05 of ISO any-accept, and SERIAL-PICK within 0.05 of POOL0-PICK. Core (relative judgment) account: POOL0-noPICK still >= ISO + 0.10, and SERIAL-noPICK < SERIAL-PICK by less than the simultaneous-vs-serial gap.
kill_criterion: Pre-specified primary: paired-by-problem difference D = choose(POOL0-noPICK) - anyaccept(ISO). Core effect KILLED (format artifact confirmed) if the 95% CI upper bound of D < 0.05 on 120 problems. Core effect CONFIRMED as format-independent if D >= 0.10 with one-sided Wilcoxon/McNemar p < 0.01. Secondary: format main effect = choose(PICK arms) - choose(noPICK arms) averaged over presentation; presentation main effect analogous; whichever exceeds the other by >= 0.08 is named the driver.
smallest_experiment: Items: 120 problems = 48 (08/x1 bank, seed 2027) + 72 (x1c bank, seed 31337), 4 wrong + 1 gold each, reusing problems.json. Arms (haiku, isolated claude -p, 1 call per unit): ISO (5 calls/problem, 600), POOL0-PICK (x1 wording), POOL0-noPICK (ACCEPT/REJECT only, same wording otherwise), SERIAL-PICK and SERIAL-noPICK (the 4 wrongs as numbered independent entries in one prompt), each in 2 random orders (4 arms x 2 x 120 = 960), plus POOL1-PICK/POOL1-noPICK one order for recall cost (240). Total about 1,800 haiku calls. Sonnet replication of the 4 POOL0 arms + ISO on the 48-problem bank: 48x(4x1)+240 = about 430 sonnet calls (trim ISO to the 4 wrongs: 384).
why_it_matters: If the PICK demand is the cause, the corpus headline ('show candidates one at a time') is mislabelled: the cheap fix is 'never ask a verifier to choose', and the eyewitness relative-judgment bridge claimed in paper.md sec. 4.5 rests on a confound. If D survives, the mechanism claim becomes genuinely presentation-based for the first time in this corpus.
scoop_risk: Low to moderate. MCQ failure-to-abstain (arXiv 2409.00113, 2402.01349, cited in paper.md sec. 2) is adjacent: it shows forced-choice formats suppress NONE, but not the presentation x format crossing in accept/reject verifiers.

hypothesis: Pooled false accepts are a correct application of the x1 'rule out the obvious alternatives' criterion to a different evidential context: shown next to visibly refuted rivals, a wrong hypothesis does rule out the displayed alternatives. Replacing the criterion with a rival-independent one ('every claim in the hypothesis is consistent with the data') removes most of the pool-minus-ISO gap, and showing rivals as non-judged context (exposure only, single verdict) reproduces it.
gap_with_citations: exp/x1-sequential-lineup/build.py HEAD (reused verbatim by x1s, x1f, x1c per x1c FINDING.md): 'Be strict: ACCEPT only if the data clearly support it and clearly rule out the obvious alternatives.' In ISO the alternatives are implicit; in POOL0 they are on screen and each is contradicted by the data. x1b FINDING.md: the same wrong hypothesis is rated +0.25 points higher (1..7) inside a target-absent pool than alone (Wilcoxon p = 0.00026) and 1.54 inside a target-present pool vs 1.71 target-absent, consistent with 'support relative to displayed rivals'. x6 ISO also uses a comparative-sounding criterion ('the main hypothesis that this study's evidence supports'). No corpus arm separates criterion wording or rival exposure from the demand to judge each rival.
prediction: Criterion account: under the absolute criterion, POOL0 choosing minus ISO any-accept shrinks by >= 50% relative to the x1 wording; the EXPOSURE arm (rivals shown, 'for context only', one verdict on the target hypothesis) yields a per-candidate accept rate close to the per-candidate POOL0 rate. Relative-judgment account: gap persists under the absolute criterion (shrink < 25%).
kill_criterion: Let G_x1 and G_abs be paired pool-minus-ISO choosing gaps under the two criteria (same problems, same orders). Criterion artifact CONFIRMED if G_abs <= 0.5 x G_x1 and the 95% bootstrap CI of (G_x1 - G_abs) excludes 0. Criterion artifact KILLED if G_abs >= 0.75 x G_x1 or G_abs >= 0.10 absolute. Exposure secondary: per-candidate accept in EXPOSURE >= ISO + 0.03 with McNemar p < 0.05 counts as 'mere exposure suffices'.
smallest_experiment: Items: the 120 synthetic problems of F1 (48 + 72). Arms (haiku): ISO-x1 and ISO-abs (4 wrongs each, 960 calls), POOL0-x1 and POOL0-abs (1 order, 240), EXPOSURE-abs (each wrong as target with its 3 sibling wrongs shown as context, 480). About 1,680 haiku calls. If the gap shrinks, a 48-problem sonnet check of POOL0-abs vs ISO-abs: about 240 sonnet calls.
why_it_matters: Separates an instruction-semantics artifact (fixable by wording) from a general relative-judgment bias. Co-scientist ranking prompts routinely include 'compared with alternatives' criteria, so either outcome is directly actionable.
scoop_risk: Low. Prompt-sensitivity of LLM judges is widely reported, but the specific comparative-criterion explanation for target-absent inflation is not tested anywhere in the corpus or in the prior art the corpus red team listed (redteam/VERDICTS.md).

hypothesis: The hypotheses that pools 'falsely' pick are not uniformly wrong: they are the most data-defensible wrong candidates (near-misses or partially true), and on a bank where every wrong candidate is certified contradicted by a specific data value, the target-absent pool-minus-ISO gap falls below 0.03.
gap_with_citations: Errors are strongly item-driven: x1c FINDING.md S2, the same wrong hypothesis is picked in 27/34 order pairs (one pair per problem 11/14 vs chance 0.25); x1s FINDING.md 9/9 same pick across orders. x4 FINDING.md documents two 'wrong' items (P017_W2, P029_W2) that are 'arguably defensible from 3 points' and accounts for all remaining false accepts. x6 FINDING.md limitation: benchmark negatives 'not independently verified as false'; VERIFICATION.md: 'No human check of the ResearchBench negatives being truly false rather than merely unpublished.' 08 FINDING.md sec. 4 example P002 shows a picked interaction hypothesis whose falsity rests on 21.1 vs 20.9 'within noise'. Family gradient: threshold family (most visually unambiguous) shows almost no effect (08: 0/12; x1c: 0.056).
prediction: Defensibility account: (a) opus/fable blind defensibility ratings (1..7, data + hypothesis only) of picked wrongs exceed never-picked wrongs by >= 1.0 point; (b) on a regenerated 'certified-contradicted' bank (each wrong asserts a quantitative claim falsified by a named cell beyond 3x the noise SD, checked programmatically), POOL0 choosing <= ISO any-accept + 0.03. Core account: choosing gap on the certified bank >= 0.10.
kill_criterion: Primary: paired gap G_cert = choose(POOL0) - anyaccept(ISO) on the certified bank, 96 problems, 3 orders averaged. Artifact CONFIRMED (core effect killed for genuinely wrong hypotheses) if the 95% CI upper bound of G_cert < 0.05. Core CONFIRMED if G_cert >= 0.10 with one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.01. Secondary (a) pre-specified threshold: mean defensibility difference picked minus never-picked >= 1.0 with Mann-Whitney p < 0.01.
smallest_experiment: Part A (re-analysis + adjudication): all distinct wrong hypotheses from x1, x1s, x1c POOL0 (192 + 288 = 480 candidates), each rated once by opus blind to pick status: 480 opus calls (or 240 by sampling all picked + an equal random never-picked set). Part B: new generator variant of gen_problems.py (4 families) with certified-contradicted wrongs, 96 problems; haiku arms ISO (384), POOL0 x 3 orders (288), POOL1 x 1 (96): 768 haiku calls. Sonnet POOL0 + ISO on 48 problems: 240 sonnet calls.
why_it_matters: If the pool only promotes defensible near-misses, the corpus claim 'the judge accepts a falsehood' becomes 'the judge relaxes its strictness threshold for the best-supported candidate', a much weaker and partly rational behaviour; the safety framing of the selection curse would need rewriting.
scoop_risk: Low. This is an internal validity check on a corpus-specific bank; no external work audits these items.

hypothesis: The real-data lineup effect (x6/x6f) generalizes beyond 9 clustered papers: on human-labeled SciFact claim-abstract pairs, where the unsupported claims are certified by annotators (CONTRADICT, or not-entailed claims from other abstracts), target-absent pools of 4 unsupported claims are chosen at least 0.10 more often than the isolated any-accept rate, with the test run at the abstract level.
gap_with_citations: x6 FINDING.md: 30 items from 9 papers ('the item-level p overstates independence'), row-level McNemar p = 0.031 on 6 of 10 rows. VERIFICATION.md: 'the effective n is nearer 10 than 30 and the item-level p-values are anticonservative', gold leaks verbatim from the abstract in 3 of 10 papers, negatives never human-checked. x6f FINDING.md: Fable 10/29 vs 0/29, same 9 papers. README.md calls real data at scale the decisive test, but full ResearchBench sits on gated Hugging Face, which is blocked here. SciFact data are reachable over plain HTTPS (I confirmed the release tarball URL scifact.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/release/latest/data.tar.gz returns 200 through the proxy; github.com/allenai/scifact is the repo).
prediction: Core account: on >= 80 distinct abstracts, POOL0 choosing minus ISO any-accept >= 0.10, positive in a majority of abstracts with any discordance. Clustering/leakage-artifact account: gap < 0.05 once items are independent and negatives are certified.
kill_criterion: Unit = abstract (one pool per abstract, so no clustering). Core KILLED on real data if the paired gap 95% CI upper bound < 0.05 (n >= 80 abstracts). CONFIRMED if gap >= 0.10 and exact McNemar one-sided p < 0.01. Pre-specified moderator: gap computed separately for pools containing a same-abstract CONTRADICT claim vs only other-abstract claims; reported, not used for the verdict.
smallest_experiment: Items: 100 SciFact abstracts that have a human SUPPORT claim and at least one human CONTRADICT claim (exact count to be read from the release files; if fewer than 100 qualify, use all). Candidates per abstract: the SUPPORT claim (gold), its CONTRADICT claim(s), and fillers from other abstracts' claims to reach 4 unsupported. Arms (haiku): ISO on 4 unsupported + gold (500), POOL0 x 2 orders (200), POOL1 x 1 (100): 800 haiku calls, using the x6 prompt wording with 'claim' for 'hypothesis'. Sonnet: POOL0 x1 + ISO on 50 abstracts (250 calls). Fable: POOL0 x1 + ISO on 40 abstracts (200 calls).
why_it_matters: Turns the corpus's only real-data evidence (n effectively about 10 papers) into a human-certified, unclustered test. A null here would confine the lineup effect to synthetic and benchmark-distractor items.
scoop_risk: Moderate: SciFact is a standard claim-verification set and listwise vs pointwise claim verification may have been compared, but not in the target-absent pool vs isolated design to my knowledge (not verified by search in this run).

hypothesis: Target-absent choosing is gated by the judge's own competence on the item: on arithmetic items the judge solves correctly when asked alone (3 of 3 samples), zero-correct pools are chosen at <= 0.10, whereas on unsolved items choosing is high; the 'lineup law' is uncertainty resolution toward the most plausible candidate, not relative judgment that overrides knowledge.
gap_with_citations: Frontier run judges must 'check everything in your head' (judge_prompts.md) and the same tier's solvers score 0.17 to 0.68 solo (paper.md sec. 3), so many items are beyond the judge. paper.md sec. 4.6 argues against a competence account only at family level (combinatorics iso f 0.0208 vs pooled 0.1469 in results_fn.txt) without item-level solve status. Choosing is flat at about 0.70 across n = 2..8 (results_fn.txt: 0.797, 0.707, 0.706, 0.699), which a constant per-item 'can't solve, pick closest' rate would also produce. In the hypothesis domain, an x1 POOL0A raw output (P000) shows the judge naming the true law ('not among the four proposed') and answering NONE, consistent with gating.
prediction: Competence account: choose(zc pools | judge solves item 3/3) <= 0.10 and choose(zc | solves 0/3) >= 0.6; picked candidate equals the judge's own (wrong) free answer, or is the numerically nearest candidate to it, in >= 50% of picks. Relative-judgment account: choose(zc | solved 3/3) >= 0.30.
kill_criterion: Primary: choosing rate in zero-correct pools restricted to items the judge solves 3/3 in separate free-answer calls. Competence-gating CONFIRMED (and the 'judge behaves as if one answer must be right' reading killed) if this rate's 95% Wilson upper bound < 0.15. Relative-judgment CONFIRMED if the rate >= 0.30 with Wilson lower bound > 0.15. Requires >= 20 solved-3/3 items; if fewer, add items from the generator until met.
smallest_experiment: Items: the 72 frontier problems (problems.json, seed 4242) plus 72 fresh items from gen_problems.py to ensure >= 20 solved items. Haiku: free-answer solve x3 per item (432), zero-correct pools at n = 2 and 5 rebuilt from pools.json candidates, 1 call per pool, 2 orders (576), isolated verdicts on the n = 5 members (720). About 1,730 haiku calls. Sonnet: solve x1 + zc n = 5 x 1 order on 72 items (144 calls).
why_it_matters: If choosing only occurs where the judge cannot solve the item, the corpus's deployment claim (a verifier 'endorses one roughly seven times out of ten regardless of batch size', paper.md sec. 4.3) becomes a statement about judge competence, and the remedy is a stronger or tool-using judge, not presentation.
scoop_risk: Low. Self-consistency between a model's own answer and its verification is studied, but not as the gate of target-absent choosing.

hypothesis: The frontier-run arm contrasts are inflated by multi-item batching: verdicts within one judge instance are overdispersed (an instance adopts a lenient or strict stance), so with one isolated call per pool and per candidate the zero-correct choosing rate at n = 2 drops to within 0.15 of the independence prediction computed from single-call isolated f.
gap_with_citations: results_addendum.txt: the isolated arm is a mixture, 2 of 12 instances accept 76/110 and 57/110 while the median slice accepts 0.0455 (min 0.0091). My recount of raw/judge_pooled_p*.txt (grep of '-zc' lines): PICK=NONE in zero-correct pools ranges from 0/27 (p2_01) to 14/18 (p1_01) across slices, 156/570 overall, so the pooled arm has the same instance heterogeneity. Serial arm: only 6 instances, 14/1152 accepts total (raw/judge_serial_*: 4,1,0,1,2,6), stricter than even the median isolated slice, which a lucky draw of strict instances could produce. paper.md sec. 6 concedes 'arm contrasts include between-instance variance'. x1 later fixed this for hypotheses (one call per pool) but the arithmetic f(n) curve and flat 0.7 choosing were never rerun with single calls.
prediction: Batching account: single-call zc choosing at n = 2 <= independence prediction 1-(1-f_iso,single)^2 + 0.15; between-slice variance in batched replication exceeds binomial by a dispersion factor >= 3 while single-call variance across random 'pseudo-slices' does not. Core account: single-call zc choosing at n = 2 and 5 stays >= 0.5 and within 0.1 of each other.
kill_criterion: Primary: single-call choosing rate at n = 2 in zero-correct pools vs the independence prediction from single-call isolated f. Core lineup law CONFIRMED under single calls if choose(n=2) - prediction >= 0.25 (CI lower > 0.15). Batching artifact CONFIRMED if choose(n=2) - prediction < 0.15 (CI upper). Secondary: overdispersion ratio of slice-level accept rates in a batched replication (12 slices of 48) vs binomial; >= 3 counts as instance stance.
smallest_experiment: Items: 72 frontier problems, candidates from pools.json. Haiku single calls: isolated verdict for each candidate appearing in zc n = 2 and n = 5 pools (about 72 x 5 = 360), zc pools n = 2 and n = 5 x 2 orders (288), serial_8 single-prompt probe re-run as 12 instances (12 calls), batched replication of the zc n = 5 pools in 12 slices of 12 pools (12 calls). About 680 haiku calls. Sonnet: zc n = 2 and n = 5, 1 order, plus isolated n = 5 members on 36 items: 252 calls.
why_it_matters: The 0.7 flat choosing rate and the 0.012 serial mitigation are the corpus's most quoted numbers and both come from 6 to 27 batched instances. If they shrink under single calls, the paper's 'lineup law' is partly a property of batch judging, itself a common deployment pattern worth naming separately.
scoop_risk: Low. Batch-judging order and carryover effects are discussed in the LLM-as-judge literature, but this specific re-estimate is internal to the corpus.

hypothesis: The flat per-pool choosing rate across pool size is an artifact of answer uniqueness in arithmetic (at most one string can be right, so per-candidate f = choosing/n is nearly an identity); for non-exclusive natural-language claims, target-absent any-accept rises with pool size (n = 2 to 8) rather than staying flat.
gap_with_citations: Flatness is measured only on arithmetic (results_fn.txt per-pool any false accept 0.797, 0.707, 0.706, 0.699 at n = 2, 3, 5, 8; paper.md sec. 6: 'no natural-language or open-ended tasks'). The 0.8/n dilution follows if the judge accepts at most one candidate per pool, which exact-answer problems invite. The paper itself flags that the flat-choosing description 'was adopted after seeing the data' and calls for a confirmatory replication with choosing rate as primary. Every hypothesis experiment (08, x1, x1c, x1s, x1f, x6) uses pools of size 4 only (08 FINDING.md sec. 6: 'no f(n) curve').
prediction: Uniqueness account: on SciFact-style claims (several can be simultaneously unsupported or supported), choose(n=8) - choose(n=2) >= 0.15 and mean accepts per choosing pool > 1.2 at n = 8. Lineup-law account: |choose(n=8) - choose(n=2)| <= 0.10 and accepts per choosing pool about 1.
kill_criterion: Primary slope of per-pool any-accept on log2(n) for n in {2, 4, 8}, item-level paired. Lineup-law flatness KILLED for natural language if choose(8) - choose(2) >= 0.15 with 95% CI lower bound > 0.05. Flatness CONFIRMED if the 95% CI of choose(8) - choose(2) lies within [-0.10, +0.10].
smallest_experiment: Items: 80 SciFact abstracts (same source as F4), 8 unsupported claims each (CONTRADICT where available plus other-abstract claims). Haiku: pools of n = 2, 4, 8 drawn as nested subsets, 2 orders (480 calls), isolated verdicts on all 8 (640 calls). About 1,120 haiku calls. Sonnet: n = 2 and 8, 1 order, on 40 abstracts plus isolated on those 8 x 40: 400 sonnet calls (trim to 4 isolated per abstract: 240).
why_it_matters: The deployment advice in paper.md sec. 5 ('per-pool false-accept probability near 0.7 whenever the pool lacks a correct answer ... at every n') is extrapolated to hypothesis pipelines. If choosing grows with n for claims, larger hypothesis batches are worse than the corpus says; if it is flat, the law generalizes.
scoop_risk: Moderate: MCQ option scaling (arXiv 2604.14634, cited in paper.md) studies accuracy vs option count, but with a correct option present and not in accept/reject target-absent mode.

hypothesis: Fable's near-immunity on the synthetic bank and its 10/29 choosing on ResearchBench are both explained by one item-level variable, the judge's isolated support margin for the most plausible wrong candidate: once items are binned by isolated margin, haiku, sonnet and fable choosing rates fall on a common curve (model main effect < 0.05), so 'capability removes the effect only where the task is easy' is a difficulty effect, not a capability effect.
gap_with_citations: x1f results.txt: Fable POOL0A choosing 2/48 = 0.042 and f_iso 0/192 on the synthetic bank; x6f FINDING.md: Fable 10/29 vs 0/29 on 9 ResearchBench papers and the reading 'Capability removes the effect only where the task is easy'. x1s FINDING.md: Sonnet 13/47 order A, no safer than haiku when the target is absent. README.md lists 'a hypothesis bank hard enough that Fable is off the ceiling' as the HIGHEST-priority next experiment. x1b gives the tool: 1..7 support ratings move with context (+0.25 inside target-absent pools). No experiment conditions on per-item difficulty across models.
prediction: Margin account: in a logistic model of choosing on (binned max isolated rating of the pool's wrongs) + model, the model term changes predicted choosing by < 0.05 at matched margin. Capability account: at matched margin, fable chooses >= 0.10 less than haiku.
kill_criterion: Primary: difference in choosing between fable and haiku at matched isolated-margin bins (inverse-variance weighted across bins with >= 8 pools per model). Difficulty-only account CONFIRMED if |diff| < 0.05 with 95% CI within [-0.08, +0.08]. KILLED (genuine capability effect) if fable - haiku <= -0.10 with CI upper bound < -0.03.
smallest_experiment: Items: 96 synthetic problems from gen_problems.py with a noise-level parameter swept over 4 levels (24 per level) so isolated margins span the range. Per model: isolated 1..7 rating of 4 wrongs (384 calls) + POOL0 1 order (96). Haiku 480 calls; sonnet 480 calls is too many, so sonnet and fable each on 48 problems (12 per level): 240 calls each. Total about 480 haiku + 480 larger-model calls.
why_it_matters: Decides whether better judges solve the lineup problem (capability) or merely move the frontier of items where it bites (difficulty). This changes the corpus's recommended remedy and the forecast for frontier co-scientists.
scoop_risk: Low. Item-difficulty conditioning of judge bias across a model family is not reported in the corpus or the cited prior art.

hypothesis: The corpus's MAS nulls (debate does not amplify false acceptance; tournaments create no winner's curse) are floor artifacts: on a bank where haiku's isolated false-accept rate is 0.15 to 0.40, one round of 3-agent debate raises majority false-accept on wrong items, and REJECT-to-ACCEPT flips on wrong items reach at least half the rate observed on gold items.
gap_with_citations: x4 FINDING.md: round-1 majority FAR already 2/96 = 2.1%; 'the conformity question is essentially untestable at this base rate'; truth-asymmetric flips 9/64 on gold vs 0/280 on wrong (Fisher p = 1.6e-7). x3 FINDING.md: haiku isolated-accepts 0/64 wrong hypotheses on the tournament problems, so 'selection cannot lift a rate that is zero for every member'; tournament pipeline 0/16 vs simultaneous 4/16 (p = 0.125). Both explicitly call for a harder bank with nonzero isolated false accepts; neither was run.
prediction: Floor account: on the hard bank, wrong-item REJECT-to-ACCEPT flip rate >= 0.5 x gold-item flip rate, and majority FAR after debate exceeds round 1 by >= 0.05. Truth-asymmetry account (x4 survives): wrong-item flip rate <= 0.25 x gold-item rate and majority FAR does not rise (difference < 0.02).
kill_criterion: Primary: ratio R = flip(R->A | wrong) / flip(R->A | gold), agent-level, on items with a split round-1 vote. Truth-asymmetry CONFIRMED (floor artifact killed) if R <= 0.25 with bootstrap 95% CI upper < 0.5. Floor artifact CONFIRMED if R >= 0.5 with CI lower > 0.25. Secondary: post-minus-pre majority FAR on wrong items, McNemar, >= +0.05 counts as amplification.
smallest_experiment: Items: build the hard bank by screening: generate 200 near-miss wrong hypotheses with gen_problems.py variants (higher noise, fewer cells), run 1 isolated haiku verdict each (200 calls), keep 96 with plausible nonzero accept (re-sampled x2 to estimate rate, 192 calls), plus 48 gold. Debate: x4 protocol, 3 haiku agents, 1 round: 144 items x 6 calls = 864. Tournament secondary (x3 protocol on 16 problems where all wrongs have nonzero isolated accept): 368 calls. About 1,620 haiku calls; no larger-model calls needed (optional sonnet debate on 48 items: 288).
why_it_matters: These two nulls are the corpus's evidence that MAS interaction (debate, pairwise tournaments) is safe; if they only hold at a floor, the safety claim for co-scientist ranking agents is unsupported exactly where it matters.
scoop_risk: Moderate: debate conformity and majority-pressure effects are reported (corpus/05 research-brief cites Wu et al. arXiv 2511.07784 on majority pressure suppressing correction), but not the truth-asymmetry ratio as a function of base false-accept rate.
